quote: In 1918, Landau proved that there is a constant c > 0 such that for any distinct primitive real characters χ₁, χ₂ to moduli q₁, q₂, at most one of L(s, χ₁) and L(s, χ₂) has an exceptional zero β > 1 −c/ log q₁q₂.
note: The concept of exceptional zeros (later called Siegel zeros or Landau-Siegel zeros) was introduced by Landau in 1918. Carl Ludwig Siegel improved the bounds on these zeros in 1935-1936. The problem of whether such zeros actually exist remains open.
